routes.label: Split the octahedron into two pyramids

question: A regular octahedron is formed by joining the centers of adjoining faces of a cube. The ratio of the volume of the octahedron to the volume of the cube is
solution:
Let the cube have side length \(s>0\), and regard one pair of opposite faces as the top and bottom. The centers of the four side faces lie in the horizontal plane halfway up the cube and form a square.

Join the center of this square to its four vertices. This divides the square into four right triangles. Each triangle has perpendicular legs of length \(s/2\), coming from two perpendicular directions from the cube's center to side-face centers. Thus the square's area is
\[
A=4\left(\frac12\cdot\frac{s}{2}\cdot\frac{s}{2}\right)
=\frac{s^2}{2}.
\]
The top and bottom face centers are the apices of two square pyramids sharing this square as their base. Together these pyramids fill the octahedron without interior overlap. Each has perpendicular height \(s/2\).

A pyramid's volume is one third of its base area times its height, so
\[
V_{\text{octahedron}}
=2\left(\frac13\cdot\frac{s^2}{2}\cdot\frac{s}{2}\right)
=\frac{s^3}{6}.
\]
The cube's volume is \(s^3\). Therefore the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{s^3/6}{s^3}=\boxed{\frac16},
\]
choice C.
